strings.name: Ursula von der Leyen
strings.role: President of the European Commission · European governance
strings.summary: Von der Leyen moved from medicine and public health into German politics, leading the family, labour and defence ministries. She became the first woman president of the European Commission in 2019 and secured a second term in 2024. Her Commission proposed the European Green Deal and coordinated digital, industrial and security policy. These policies involve EU institutions and member states collectively, rather than one individual alone.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 13 November 2026; selected career milestones cover 1958–2026. Her latest official profile and the 2026 State of the Union address confirm her role and living status. Announcing policy does not mean its goals have been achieved.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Hanover Medical School: medical licence, 1987; doctorate, 1991; Master of Public Health, 2001
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: European institutional leadership
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Became the first woman Commission president in 2019 and again secured European Parliament support in 2024.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: European Green Deal
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Her Commission proposed the Green Deal in 2019 as a cross-sector framework for climate and economic transition.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Delivers State of the Union address
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Outlined priorities for the coming year in the European Parliament, covering competitiveness, security, climate and social issues.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Second Commission takes office
strings.timeline.event-02.text: After her July re-election by Parliament, the new Commission began its term in December.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Presents the European Green Deal
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The Commission published a climate and economic-transition framework for subsequent EU legislation and investment.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Becomes Commission president
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Became the first woman in the role, moving from German federal politics to EU executive leadership.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Becomes German defence minister
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Moved from labour and social affairs to defence, serving until 2019.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Becomes labour and social affairs minister
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Led federal employment and social affairs policy until 2013.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Joins the federal cabinet
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Became minister for family affairs, senior citizens, women and youth, moving from state to federal government.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Becomes a Lower Saxony minister
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Took responsibility for social affairs, women, families and health at state level.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Qualifies as a physician
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Completed medical studies in Hanover, then undertook clinical and research work and earned doctoral and public-health qualifications.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Brussels
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Belgium, later educated in Germany before entering medicine and public service.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads the European Commission and participates in shaping Europe’s green transition, digital regulation, pandemic recovery and geopolitical policy.
